questions.title: Extract a country code
questions.prompt: In Case 2, A2 contains JAP1080-19M. Write a formula that extracts the three-character location code and state the result.
questions.answer: =LEFT(A2,3) returns JAP.

criteria.label: Reusable formula extracts first three characters
Correct result JAP

questions.title: Extract a variable-length plant ID
questions.prompt: In Case 2, A2 contains JAP1080-19M. Write a formula that extracts the plant ID between the dash and the final pay-period letter. State the result.
questions.answer: =MID(A2,FIND("-",A2)+1,LEN(A2)-FIND("-",A2)-1) returns 19. Other correct formulas accepted.

criteria.label: Finds dash dynamically
Excludes final pay-period letter
Correct result 19

questions.title: Construct a composite identifier
questions.prompt: Location is in D2 and PlantID is in F2. Write a formula producing Location-PlantID, such as JAP-19.

criteria.label: Combines correct cells
Uses hyphen separator

questions.title: Avoid fixed-width extraction
questions.prompt: Case 3 uses codes such as Japan177-3Mo and AUS551-2Mo. Explain why LEFT(A2,3) is unsuitable for extracting the location in every row, and describe a repeatable alternative.
questions.answer: Country codes vary in length. Locate the first numeric character, then take all characters before it (e.g. LEFT with MIN/FIND over digits). Test across all country codes; do not hard-code each row.

criteria.label: Identifies variable-length codes and failure on Japan
Reusable first-digit extraction method

questions.title: Standardise pay periods
questions.prompt: In Case 3, W and We both mean weekly; M and Mo both mean monthly. Describe how to standardise these values without altering the original EmployeeCode.
questions.answer: Create a derived PayPeriod field, extract trailing letters, map W/We to Weekly and M/Mo to Monthly. Retain original code, flag unexpected values.

criteria.label: Correctly maps both pairs
Derived field and validation of unexpected codes

questions.title: Join on the right key
questions.prompt: Case 4 reuses PreparerID across business units. Explain how to attach the correct PreparerName to a journal line, and why matching only PreparerID is unsafe.
questions.answer: Match both BusinessUnitID and PreparerID using a composite-key or multi-criteria lookup. PreparerID alone is not unique and may return the wrong employee. Validate unmatched and duplicate keys.

criteria.label: Uses both key fields
Explains non-uniqueness and checks matches

questions.title: A lookup to the left
questions.prompt: In Case 4, ChartOfAccounts contains GLAccountName in column A and GLAccountNumber in column B, rows 2:86. A journal line has GLAccountNumber in B2. Write a formula to return the account name.
questions.answer: =INDEX(ChartOfAccounts!$A$2:$A$86,MATCH(B2,ChartOfAccounts!$B$2:$B$86,0)) or equivalent exact-match XLOOKUP.

criteria.label: Matches GLAccountNumber exactly
Returns GLAccountName using reusable ranges

questions.title: Check an ETL join
questions.prompt: After adding reference data to the 789 journal lines in Case 4, what checks would you perform before using the joined file?
questions.answer: Reconcile row count to 789, check no one-to-many join duplication, reconcile Amount/debit/credit totals, investigate missing reference matches and duplicate reference keys.

criteria.label: Row count and duplicate-key checks
Reconciles amounts and investigates unmatched rows

questions.title: Make wages comparable
questions.prompt: Explain how to make the 2015 and 2016 payroll wage fields comparable in IntegrateCo.
questions.answer: 2015 gross wages = Reg_Pay + OT_Pay; 2016 uses Gross_Wages. Map Emp_No to Employee_Number, aggregate to common employee/job/half-year level; retain year. Do not double count overtime.

criteria.label: Correct gross-wage mapping without double counting
Common aggregation and stable employee identifier

questions.title: Preserve job codes
questions.prompt: Why should job code 001 be retained as text, and why is treating the entire 2015 Job field as the job code incorrect?
questions.answer: Three-character text preserves leading zeros. Job includes project year, optional department, three-digit job code and optional location. Extract the code and validate against 001–012.

criteria.label: Leading-zero preservation
Explains compound field and extracts/validates code

questions.title: Monthly comparisons
questions.prompt: Can the provided 2016 payroll file support an actual monthly wage comparison with 2015? Explain.
questions.answer: No: 2016 has no dates and is aggregated by employee/project/department/location. A monthly allocation based on 2015 is an estimate with an explicit stable-seasonality assumption, not observed monthly 2016 wages.

criteria.label: Recognises missing dates and different granularity
Distinguishes estimated allocation and its assumption

questions.title: Zero-hour observations
questions.prompt: How would you handle job codes with no wages or hours in one year when preparing the overall job-code table and comparing pay per hour?
questions.answer: Retain all valid job codes in the overall table using the job-code reference list. Avoid division by zero; display N/A or explain IFERROR. Do not interpret absent comparable hours as a real zero wage rate.

criteria.label: Retains all valid reference job codes
Handles zero denominator and comparability

questions.title: Missing employee numbers
questions.prompt: How many 2016 payroll rows have a missing Employee_Number? Enter a number.

criteria.label: Correct result from supplied payroll file

questions.title: Wages without an employee number
questions.prompt: What is the sum of Gross_Wages for 2016 rows with missing Employee_Number? Round to two decimals.

criteria.label: Correct result from supplied payroll file

questions.title: P-card red flags
questions.prompt: An OSU cardholder makes two same-day purchases from the same vendor: $3,100 and $2,400. Explain a useful audit test and the conclusion you can draw from this pattern.
questions.answer: Group by cardholder, vendor and date; identify multiple purchases each below $5,000 but with combined amount above $5,000. Here combined amount is $5,500. Flag possible split purchasing; examine receipts, purpose and approvals before concluding intent or a violation.

criteria.label: Correct grouping and threshold test
5500 total and cautious evidence-based conclusion

questions.title: Design a prohibited-purchase test
questions.prompt: Describe how you would search OSU P-card transactions for prohibited gift cards and explain why a keyword match alone is insufficient evidence of a violation.
questions.answer: Search Description/Vendor/MCC for relevant gift-card indicators, account for spelling and wording, review invoices and business purpose. Keyword hits may be false positives and misses may be false negatives; a red flag is not a proven violation.

criteria.label: Uses relevant fields and documented screening logic
Explains limitations and corroborating evidence

questions.title: Predict daily sales
questions.prompt: Using the displayed basic model, predict daily netTotal when tmax=60 and gameDay=1. Enter a number rounded to two decimals.

criteria.label: Correct intercept plus both predictor contributions

questions.title: Interpret temperature
questions.prompt: Interpret the tmax coefficient in the basic model, keeping its units and the other variable in mind.
questions.answer: A one-unit increase in tmax is associated with a 7.3130 currency-unit change in predicted daily netTotal, holding gameDay constant. Association, not proof of causation.

criteria.label: Correct direction, magnitude and units
Holds gameDay constant and avoids causal overclaim

questions.title: Interpret a game-day indicator
questions.prompt: Interpret the gameDay coefficient in the basic model and identify its reference group.
questions.answer: At the same tmax, a game day (1) has predicted daily sales 1421.3360 currency units different from a non-game day (0). This is conditional association.

criteria.label: Correct game vs non-game comparison and coefficient
Holds temperature constant; avoids causal assertion

questions.title: Significance and business importance
questions.prompt: Using the basic model, assess tmax at a 5% significance level. Explain what its p-value does and does not establish.
questions.answer: tmax p=0.00758994. Compare with .05 to decide rejection of zero coefficient under model assumptions. A p-value is not probability the null is true, not an effect size, and not proof of causality. Economic relevance depends on coefficient magnitude and context.

criteria.label: Correct decision using displayed p-value and 5% threshold
Distinguishes statistical, economic and causal interpretation

questions.title: Interpret an interaction
questions.prompt: In the interaction model, state the slope on netTotal_364 for non-game days and game days, and explain the interaction coefficient.
questions.answer: Non-game slope=0.619594; game-day slope=0.630334. Interaction coefficient=0.010740 is difference between those slopes; it is not a constant overall game-day effect.

criteria.label: Correct two conditional slopes
Interaction interpreted as slope difference

questions.title: Communicate forecast uncertainty
questions.prompt: Bob wants a forecast seven days ahead. Explain why a fitted value from these restaurant models alone is insufficient, and what else you would communicate.
questions.answer: Need future predictor values or explicit assumptions. Report prediction uncertainty, model limits and out-of-sample/time-aware validation. Residual variability and future predictor uncertainty remain; high R-squared does not guarantee accuracy. Observed relationships are not necessarily causal.

criteria.label: Future inputs or explicit assumptions required
Prediction uncertainty and time-aware validation

questions.title: Prepare daily regression data
questions.prompt: Explain how to merge the restaurant sales, weather and game data without accidentally duplicating observations or inflating sales totals.
questions.answer: Aggregate product-level sales to one daily netTotal first; verify one row per date in weather and games; join by date; code missing game flags as zero only after confirming the game list is complete. Check daily uniqueness, missing weather and reconciled sales totals.

criteria.label: Common daily granularity and valid date joins
Uniqueness, missing data and reconciliation checks

schemas.songs:
CREATE TABLE songs (
    id INTEGER,
    name TEXT,
    artist_id INTEGER,
    danceability REAL,
    energy REAL,
    key INTEGER,
    loudness REAL,
    speechiness REAL,
    valence REAL,
    tempo REAL,
    duration_ms INTEGER
)

CREATE TABLE artists (
    id INTEGER,
    name TEXT
)
schemas.chinook:
CREATE TABLE [Album]
(
    [AlbumId] INTEGER  NOT NULL,
    [Title] NVARCHAR(160)  NOT NULL,
    [ArtistId] INTEGER  NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT [PK_Album] PRIMARY KEY  ([AlbumId]),
    FOREIGN KEY ([ArtistId]) REFERENCES [Artist] ([ArtistId]) 
		ON DELETE NO ACTION ON UPDATE NO ACTION
)

CREATE TABLE [Artist]
(
    [ArtistId] INTEGER  NOT NULL,
    [Name] NVARCHAR(120),
    CONSTRAINT [PK_Artist] PRIMARY KEY  ([ArtistId])
)

CREATE TABLE [Customer]
(
    [CustomerId] INTEGER  NOT NULL,
    [FirstName] NVARCHAR(40)  NOT NULL,
    [LastName] NVARCHAR(20)  NOT NULL,
    [Company] NVARCHAR(80),
    [Address] NVARCHAR(70),
    [City] NVARCHAR(40),
    [State] NVARCHAR(40),
    [Country] NVARCHAR(40),
    [PostalCode] NVARCHAR(10),
    [Phone] NVARCHAR(24),
    [Fax] NVARCHAR(24),
    [Email] NVARCHAR(60)  NOT NULL,
    [SupportRepId] INTEGER,
    CONSTRAINT [PK_Customer] PRIMARY KEY  ([CustomerId]),
    FOREIGN KEY ([SupportRepId]) REFERENCES [Employee] ([EmployeeId]) 
		ON DELETE NO ACTION ON UPDATE NO ACTION
)

CREATE TABLE [Employee]
(
    [EmployeeId] INTEGER  NOT NULL,
    [LastName] NVARCHAR(20)  NOT NULL,
    [FirstName] NVARCHAR(20)  NOT NULL,
    [Title] NVARCHAR(30),
    [ReportsTo] INTEGER,
    [BirthDate] DATETIME,
    [HireDate] DATETIME,
    [Address] NVARCHAR(70),
    [City] NVARCHAR(40),
    [State] NVARCHAR(40),
    [Country] NVARCHAR(40),
    [PostalCode] NVARCHAR(10),
    [Phone] NVARCHAR(24),
    [Fax] NVARCHAR(24),
    [Email] NVARCHAR(60),
    CONSTRAINT [PK_Employee] PRIMARY KEY  ([EmployeeId]),
    FOREIGN KEY ([ReportsTo]) REFERENCES [Employee] ([EmployeeId]) 
		ON DELETE NO ACTION ON UPDATE NO ACTION
)

CREATE TABLE [Genre]
(
    [GenreId] INTEGER  NOT NULL,
    [Name] NVARCHAR(120),
    CONSTRAINT [PK_Genre] PRIMARY KEY  ([GenreId])
)

CREATE TABLE [Invoice]
(
    [InvoiceId] INTEGER  NOT NULL,
    [CustomerId] INTEGER  NOT NULL,
    [InvoiceDate] DATETIME  NOT NULL,
    [BillingAddress] NVARCHAR(70),
    [BillingCity] NVARCHAR(40),
    [BillingState] NVARCHAR(40),
    [BillingCountry] NVARCHAR(40),
    [BillingPostalCode] NVARCHAR(10),
    [Total] NUMERIC(10,2)  NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT [PK_Invoice] PRIMARY KEY  ([InvoiceId]),
    FOREIGN KEY ([CustomerId]) REFERENCES [Customer] ([CustomerId]) 
		ON DELETE NO ACTION ON UPDATE NO ACTION
)

CREATE TABLE [InvoiceLine]
(
    [InvoiceLineId] INTEGER  NOT NULL,
    [InvoiceId] INTEGER  NOT NULL,
    [TrackId] INTEGER  NOT NULL,
    [UnitPrice] NUMERIC(10,2)  NOT NULL,
    [Quantity] INTEGER  NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT [PK_InvoiceLine] PRIMARY KEY  ([InvoiceLineId]),
    FOREIGN KEY ([InvoiceId]) REFERENCES [Invoice] ([InvoiceId]) 
		ON DELETE NO ACTION ON UPDATE NO ACTION,
    FOREIGN KEY ([TrackId]) REFERENCES [Track] ([TrackId]) 
		ON DELETE NO ACTION ON UPDATE NO ACTION
)

CREATE TABLE [MediaType]
(
    [MediaTypeId] INTEGER  NOT NULL,
    [Name] NVARCHAR(120),
    CONSTRAINT [PK_MediaType] PRIMARY KEY  ([MediaTypeId])
)

CREATE TABLE [Playlist]
(
    [PlaylistId] INTEGER  NOT NULL,
    [Name] NVARCHAR(120),
    CONSTRAINT [PK_Playlist] PRIMARY KEY  ([PlaylistId])
)

CREATE TABLE [PlaylistTrack]
(
    [PlaylistId] INTEGER  NOT NULL,
    [TrackId] INTEGER  NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT [PK_PlaylistTrack] PRIMARY KEY  ([PlaylistId], [TrackId]),
    FOREIGN KEY ([PlaylistId]) REFERENCES [Playlist] ([PlaylistId]) 
		ON DELETE NO ACTION ON UPDATE NO ACTION,
    FOREIGN KEY ([TrackId]) REFERENCES [Track] ([TrackId]) 
		ON DELETE NO ACTION ON UPDATE NO ACTION
)

CREATE TABLE [Track]
(
    [TrackId] INTEGER  NOT NULL,
    [Name] NVARCHAR(200)  NOT NULL,
    [AlbumId] INTEGER,
    [MediaTypeId] INTEGER  NOT NULL,
    [GenreId] INTEGER,
    [Composer] NVARCHAR(220),
    [Milliseconds] INTEGER  NOT NULL,
    [Bytes] INTEGER,
    [UnitPrice] NUMERIC(10,2)  NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT [PK_Track] PRIMARY KEY  ([TrackId]),
    FOREIGN KEY ([AlbumId]) REFERENCES [Album] ([AlbumId]) 
		ON DELETE NO ACTION ON UPDATE NO ACTION,
    FOREIGN KEY ([GenreId]) REFERENCES [Genre] ([GenreId]) 
		ON DELETE NO ACTION ON UPDATE NO ACTION,
    FOREIGN KEY ([MediaTypeId]) REFERENCES [MediaType] ([MediaTypeId]) 
		ON DELETE NO ACTION ON UPDATE NO ACTION
)
